cohort: 200 pregnant women aged 18-48 years with singleton pregnancies and at least one previous live birth, attending Al-Basra Maternity and Children Hospital.
finding: Short interpregnancy interval (<18 months) is significantly associated with adverse fetal outcomes, including preterm birth, low birth weight, NICU admission, and stillbirth.
mod_finding: Delivery mode did not significantly differ between the short and longer interpregnancy interval groups.
